thesis: A sticky telecom BSS/OSS franchise with expanding operating margin (17.8% TTM) and a 10.19% FCF yield funding buybacks trades below its own 5-year minimum EV/EBITDA, EV/Sales and P/FCF, where the price implies a revenue decline that new multi-year contracts do not show.
reason: The mechanical bear value sits above the price, operating margins are expanding and cash returns are strong, so the skew is favourable. Extreme AT&T/T-Mobile concentration, falling net margin, rising leverage and earnings in two weeks hold conviction at 4, not 5. Standard volatility-scaled core size. Macro is context only.

triggers.text: TTM operating margin falls below 15%, reversing the FY2021-25 expansion from 14.0% to 17.9% and signalling pricing pressure from concentrated customers.
TTM ROIC falls below 13%, under the FY2021 five-year low of 13.9%, giving back the gains in capital efficiency.
TTM FCF margin falls below 11%, under the FY2022 five-year low of 11.6%, showing cash generation can no longer fund buybacks.
AT&T or T-Mobile discloses non-renewal, a material scope reduction or insourcing of its Amdocs relationship (20-F, 6-K or company release), or net debt/EBITDA on the ratios page rises above 1.5x.
